I calculated each part from the table: 88 freshmen (40 play a sport) and 120 seniors (35 play a sport), so 75 of the 208 students play a sport.

- **A:** P(plays a sport | freshman) = 40/88 ≈ **0.455**.
- **B:** The events are **not independent**. P(plays a sport | freshman) ≈ 0.455, but P(plays a sport) = 75/208 ≈ 0.361. Independence would need these two probabilities to be equal.
- **C:** X follows a **binomial distribution with n = 6 and p = 0.36**.
  - P(X = 0) = 0.64⁶ ≈ 0.0687
  - P(X = 1) = 6(0.36)(0.64⁵) ≈ 0.2319
  - P(X ≥ 2) = 1 − 0.0687 − 0.2319 ≈ **0.699**
- **D:** The sample proportion is p̂ = 40/88 ≈ 0.4545.
  - Standard error = √(0.4545 × 0.5455 / 88) ≈ 0.0531
  - Margin of error = 1.96 × 0.0531 ≈ 0.104
  - The 95% confidence interval is **(0.351, 0.559)**.
- **E:** We are 95% confident that the interval from 0.351 to 0.559 captures the true proportion of all freshmen who play a sport. "95% confidence" means that if we took many random samples of this size and built an interval the same way each time, about 95% of those intervals would contain the true proportion.

The item looks sound.
